No—you would not be able to spot the Moon from Perth at that moment.

Its altitude is **−51.9°**, meaning it is far below the horizon, in roughly the opposite part of the sky from where it would need to be visible. The Sun is also below the horizon, and the Moon is only **5.75% illuminated**, so even if it were above the horizon it would be a very thin, faint crescent and difficult to see in twilight or haze.

You’d need to wait until the Moon rises. Given its phase and position, it is likely to appear as a thin crescent near the **morning eastern sky** on a subsequent day, shortly before sunrise. At the stated time, though, it is physically below Perth’s horizon and cannot be seen with unaided eyes.
